item.title: Nadi resident raises concern over lack of ear and nose specialist at Lautoka Aspen
item.description: A Nadi resident is calling for an ear and nose specialist to be available at Lautoka Aspen Hospital, raising concerns that the hospital has been without a specialist for the past four months. The resident, who wished to remain anonymous, says around 60 people were waiting when he visited the hospital on Friday.
item.content:encoded:
A Nadi resident is calling for an ear and nose specialist to be available at Lautoka Aspen Hospital, raising concerns that the hospital has been without a specialist for the past four months.

The resident, who wished to remain anonymous, says around 60 people were waiting when he visited the hospital on Friday.

He says it is disappointing that patients are not receiving the services they need.

The resident says he also tried contacting the Ministry of Health, and they told him they do not know anything.

He says Aspen Hospital staff have been advising patients to travel to Suva for treatment, but not everyone can afford to travel or is well enough to make the journey to CWM Hospital.

The resident also told fijivillage News that patients are often given appointments for later dates and, at times, have to see SOPD doctors because a specialist is not available.

The resident is calling for immediate action, saying patients should not have to spend time and money travelling from Nadi to Lautoka only to find that the specialist is unavailable and they have to return on another day.

We have sent questions to the Ministry of Health.

item.title: Thakor Punja granted bail in another alleged marijuana possession case
item.description: Thakor Punja has been granted bail by the Navua Magistrates Court this morning after he was brought to court in another case of alleged marijuana possession. Punja was allegedly found with 7.14 grams of marijuana at a checkpoint in Pacific Harbour on Thursday night.
item.content:encoded:
Thakor Punja has been granted bail by the Navua Magistrates Court this morning after he was brought to court in another case of alleged marijuana possession.

Punja was allegedly found with 7.14 grams of marijuana at a checkpoint in Pacific Harbour on Thursday night.

He is charged with one count of unlawful possession of illicit drugs.

Police Prosecutor Nitesh Prasad had strongly objected to bail.

Punja has been granted bail on strict conditions, including a $1,000 bail bond, two sureties and a stop departure order.

In a separate matter, he is charged with one count each of unlawful possession of 0.84 grams of methamphetamine, 5.447 grams of cocaine and 6.6 grams of marijuana.

The trial is scheduled from November 30th to December 4th in the Suva Magistrates Court.

item.title: Uciwai residents frustrated over repeated road grading, says they need permanent solutions
item.description: Residents of Uciwai Road in Nadi say they are still waiting for a permanent solution to the road conditions, despite the Fiji Roads Authority grading the road last week. Resident Selema Evans says grading the road has not addressed the community’s main concern, which is the lack of a proper tarsealed road and the dust affecting residents, businesses and school children.
item.content:encoded:
Residents of Uciwai Road in Nadi say they are still waiting for a permanent solution to the road conditions, despite the Fiji Roads Authority grading the road last week.

Resident Selema Evans says grading the road has not addressed the community’s main concern, which is the lack of a proper tarsealed road and the dust affecting residents, businesses and school children.

Evans says the FRA graded the road last Monday after fijivillage News raised the residents’ concerns with the authority, but no further work has been carried out to provide a lasting solution.

She says residents have repeatedly raised the same concerns with the FRA over the years, but temporary repairs continue to be carried out.

Evans says the community needs a permanent solution rather than repeated grading and temporary road works.

fijivillage News is continuing to follow up with the Fiji Roads Authority on the delay in providing a permanent solution.

item.title: American Showcase to bring a taste of the US to Suva
item.description: US Embassy Public Affairs Officer Strader Payton says the free family event at Fiji Museum will feature American music, food, sports, games and a range of other activities. Payton says the event is part of celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of the United States, and will also celebrate the relationship between Fiji and the US.
item.content:encoded:
US Embassy Public Affairs Officer Strader Payton says the free family event at Fiji Museum will feature American music, food, sports, games and a range of other activities.

Payton says the event is part of celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of the United States, and will also celebrate the relationship between Fiji and the US.

He says while the two countries may appear far apart, they are connected by the Pacific Ocean and share values such as freedom and democracy.

Payton says whether people enjoy rock and roll, R&B, country music, sports or simply spending time with family, there will be something for everyone.

The American Showcase will be held at the Fiji Museum Grounds and Thurston Gardens from 10am to 5pm this Saturday.

item.title: Three more arrested over alleged aggravated robbery in Nabua
item.description: Three more men have been arrested following another raid by the Southern Division Task Force in connection with an alleged aggravated robbery at Sukanaivalu Road in Nabua yesterday. Police say the three men, aged 27, 23 and 21, were arrested during an afternoon raid.
item.content:encoded:
Three more men have been arrested following another raid by the Southern Division Task Force in connection with an alleged aggravated robbery at Sukanaivalu Road in Nabua yesterday.

Police say the three men, aged 27, 23 and 21, were arrested during an afternoon raid.

This brings the total number of arrests to four, after a man in his 20s was arrested at Sukanaivalu Road earlier in the day.

Police say the four men allegedly hired the victim’s taxi from Narere to Nabua and, after arriving at their destination, stole the driver’s watch and cash.
